events.text_en: Chung Hoài Cực gives the first weight of Thiên Quyền Thị's scales to Hề Văn Ước and makes her Chief Judge of the Compact: the one who seals does not weigh.
The Thiên Cơ Hall walks the borders of the seven great sects and plants 129 steles; from this year a line the Compact draws can be felt by anyone who crosses it.
Đỗ Tinh Hà takes the Bắc Thần Ấn at Thạch Kiều before the seals of the seven great sects; from this year the Pivot's head is confirmed by the sects whose peace he keeps.
Every guard on Tinh Tủy Mạch is called down to the plain of Chiết Kích as reinforcements; none returns, and the vein stands unwatched for three years.
The seat's half of the Thiết Mã tally is missing from Tàng Ước Các the winter after the battle; the keeper searches the shelves for a year.
The Pivot's envoy Trình Bạch Tiết is killed on the stair of Phá Quân Môn carrying his lord's refusal; from this year the Pivot's envoys carry jade tallies, never iron.
At the clearing of Hắc Phong Trại, Đỗ Tinh Hà spares the youngest of the rogues and keeps him as a hunter.
At Doãn Ngọc Hành's confirmation Thính Vũ Lâu's seal is set a day late, because its envoy is out buying grain in the drought; the same year its disciples march on Đan Sơn Mạch.
Doãn Ngọc Hành asks the Chief Judge for the Weight and judges Băng Tâm's petition himself, the first head to do so since 510; he returns the Weight the next morning.
A copy of the 803 guard roll of Tinh Tủy Mạch is handed to Băng Tâm's envoy in a guest-house at Thạch Kiều.
